target_customer: South African employers and their lower-income employees
problem: Most South African workers run out of money before month end and borrow informally at 30-50% interest.
business_model: B2B2C earned wage access and employee financial wellness platform integrated with payroll

founders.name: Simon Ward
founders.background_notes: About 25 years in fintech and ecommerce with several exits per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll integrations and wallet/voucher features; regulatory complexity more than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll integration with employers adds stickiness; unsourced.

market_need_then: Company states over 75% of 12M employed South Africans run out of money before month end and 52% borrow; unverified company claim.

identity.voice_and_tone: Professional, confident, benefit-focused ('We empower your employees to thrive')

pivots.to: Employer benefits platform with savings, pension-backed home loans, rewards and communications
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from YC description versus current site

outcome_analysis: Floatpays launched in South Africa in July 2020, joined YC in Summer 2021 and had 15 staff by the snapshot; the current site shows a broader employer benefits bundle than the original wage-access app. Funding is not verified and no outcome is public in sources reached.
notes: The YC page cites a $4M seed reported 25 Jan 2022 (a Bizcommunity headline); I could not open that article, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Current site and YC description differ (pivot entry has no date and rests on that difference). Web search budget for the session was exhausted before this shard started, so only direct page fetches were possible; outcome, funding cross-check, dated-competitor and branding searches could not be run.
